Vector retrieval answers local questions by finding nearby chunks. For “what are the main themes across the entire corpus?”, top-k similarity can overrepresent a few documents. GraphRAG extracts entities/relations, clusters the resulting graph, and summarizes communities, giving global questions a broader route to evidence. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130)

The tradeoff is extraction/summarization expense, update complexity, and compounded errors: an invented relation can contaminate summaries. Keep links from summaries to original passages and evaluate coverage/diversity alongside factuality. Use ordinary hybrid retrieval for precise local lookups and graph/community summaries for corpus-level synthesis. GraphRAG is a workload-specific complement, not a guarantee of correctness or a replacement for access control on source documents and derived summaries.
